justification: The lifting force is located in the shallow mat, not the deep soil: "her team found dense mats of fine root, thickening year on year", and Askerholt states "Most of the force, we think, is generated within a hand’s width of the stone". A is contradicted because her coring did settle where the force comes from. C overstates the deep finding — the passage says only that half a metre down "there was almost nothing alive", which leaves some life and is not the same as being bare of living root. D is never addressed; no cutting of anchoring roots during earlier repairs is mentioned.

The five streets are singled out precisely by their bedding: "They had been bedded to an older specification, on coarse sand laid nearly twice as deep as the current rule allows". B misattributes the separate single street where "a water main was renewed halfway along it, and the trench was reinstated badly". C is contradicted by "The five had one thing in common". A is contradicted because the crates did not fail — the roots were "riding clear over the crates beneath".

On the twenty-five the flags were never lifted, so only the surface has been assessed: "The surveys measure the stones, and only the stones", and Askerholt insists "We are reading the flags, not the roots". C is exactly the inference the passage refuses — "For all we know, the bedding on the good streets is filling with root that has not yet found its strength" — and B is contradicted by the stable gauge reading of "four millimetres, the same figure as the year before". D is not addressed anywhere.

The writer adjudicates in her own voice and splits the verdict against Fearnbeck on balance: "On the five streets Fearnbeck’s case is fairly won; on the twenty-five it is not". That makes C’s proportion backwards and rules out D, since she does take a side rather than merely reporting the dispute. A is contradicted because "Askerholt’s group had thought his worry overdone" is attributed to Askerholt’s group and is then partly corrected by the five streets.

The text has two movements: the mechanism of lift — "Most of the force, we think, is generated within a hand’s width of the stone" — and one city’s trial of the engineered remedy, "Thirty-one streets were rebuilt on cells", where "For seven years both sides have been surveyed every April". B is only half right: the older remedies do fail ("Each measure buys a season or two. The flags keep rising"), but the cells held on twenty-five of thirty-one streets, so a continuing failure of remedies misdescribes the second half. A is a single first-paragraph detail and D is never raised.

The frame is the fixed English collocation “it quietly takes its ___(1)___ on the general mood”, and only “toll” completes “take its toll on”. Arguing for the others: “price” and “cost” are semantically adjacent (the contest is costly), but English says “at a price” / “at a cost”, never “takes its price/cost on”; “charge” has no sense that fits a gradual drain on mood. The surrounding logic — “deciding whose is a contest nobody admits to entering” — is exactly the slow attritional damage “toll” names.

“The tone is light, but nobody misreads it; beneath the sponge the message is ___(2)___, and it is aimed at certain chairs.” The “but” demands a word that contrasts with “light”, and “aimed at certain chairs” demands directedness — both are met only by “pointed”. Arguing for the others: “relaxed” and “amused” agree with “light” instead of contrasting with it, so they kill the “but”; “spirited” means lively/energetic and describes the cartoon-sponge surface, not the targeted meaning underneath it.

“you cannot hold the moral high ___(3)___ and a dripping brush at the same time” is the idiom “hold the moral high ground”, and the joke depends on “hold” governing both “ground” and “brush”. Arguing for the others: “high horse” is a real idiom but takes “get on”/“ride”, not “hold”, and is not “moral high horse”; “hold the floor” is idiomatic but means to have the right to speak, which does not combine with “moral high”; “field” has no such expression. The context — “the first person to raise the subject has, by raising it, volunteered” — is precisely about forfeiting the high ground.

“So the kitchen waits. ___(4)___, somebody cracks”: the preceding “waits” sets up a stretch of time whose end the adverb must mark, which is “Eventually”. Arguing for the others: “Similarly” needs a parallel case and none precedes; “Presumably” hedges, but the narrator asserts the outcome with confidence (“nearly always the same somebody”), so a hedge contradicts the sentence it introduces; “Ironically” needs a reversal, whereas the person who “minds the mess a little more than the rest” cracking first is the expected outcome, not an inverted one.

“most kitchens ___(5)___ an uneasy balance between confrontation and squalor” is the collocation “strike a balance”. Arguing for the others: “land” takes a deal or a job, not a balance; “deal” takes a blow or cards; “cast” takes a vote or a shadow — none of the three licenses “a balance” as object. The sentence is a settlement between two bad poles, which is exactly what a struck balance is.

The passage states: “whatever wet reached the torching sat against the battens until they decayed along its line” — option D restates this. A inverts it (the mortar “passes damp” to timber rather than sheltering it); B is contradicted because the tiles “hang from two small lugs at the head, the nibs, hooked over each batten”, not from the mortar; C overreaches — torching stopped only “the fine snow, dust and draughts” pushed up between the tiles, and wet still reached it.

The sequence supports B: “Six pews in the middle aisle are marked vacant that year, and four the year after”, and in the 1851 plan “the vacant marks are gone” precisely because “Thin ruled lines now cut the boxes into single sittings, let at two shillings apiece, and names crowd where one household’s name used to stand” — dividing the boxes filled pews that no longer let whole. A is contradicted by the preceding vacancies; C has no support, since nothing links the sittings to the free-bench poor; D misreads the price — two shillings bought one sitting (“apiece”), not a whole box.

The passage describes slaking directly: “Möter den brända stenen sedan vatten börjar den sjuda, spricker och faller sönder till ett fint vitt mjöl.” That is A verbatim in substance — fizzing and disintegration into a white powder. Arguing for the others: B (heat igniting dry wood) is true of quicklime in reality but is nowhere in the text; C (pits for maturing) is never mentioned — the text instead says “den brända stenen förvarades torr” before slaking; D is a half-quote — “den släckta kalk som blandad med sand ger murbruk” makes the sand mixing follow slaking, and the added “medan den ännu sjöd” is unsupported.

“En ugn var för stor för ett enskilt hushåll. Den restes och brändes av ett ugnslag – en handfull grannar som sköt till var sin andel ved, turades om vid elden och delade den färdiga kalken efter insats.” That is D. Arguing for the others: A is contradicted by “för stor för ett enskilt hushåll”; B invents an owner — the kiln is collectively raised and the yield divided “efter insats”, not sold by a wealthy farm; C is contradicted outright by “Det mesta av kalken gick till avsalu.”

Both halves of B are stated: “för många hushåll var ugnen den binäring som över huvud taget gav kontanter”, and “Mot seklets slut tappade ugnslagen sin marknad … priset föll under vad ett lag av grannar kunde möta.” Arguing for the others: A inverts the text — “Framför allt var det dit kalken gick: till murningen”, while the fields got only “något”; C reverses the chronology, since burning “hade … sedan länge varit böndernas sak” with written evidence “från 1600-talets mitt” and the railway kilns ended rather than started it; D is contradicted by “Berget var däremot sällan något bekymmer.”

The inference is licensed by “inte sällan flera i rad utmed samma sluttning, äldre ugnar som övergivits när skogen omkring dem huggits ut, och som ersatts av en yngre ugn längre bort”: the seventy remains are successive replacements, so their number overstates how many kilns ran at once. Arguing for the others: A misreads “i gränsen mellan inägor och utmark”, which is a farm-internal boundary, not a parish boundary; B is contradicted by the museum rebuilding a kiln “med handbokens kapitel och Gillervalls uppmätningar som förlaga”; D is contradicted verbatim by “Hur gamla de äldsta lämningarna är går inte att avgöra utan utgrävning.”

The stem asks about the saving calculation, and the text names one flaw in it: “Vintern 2023 byttes spårets gamla kvicksilverlampor mot ledbelysning … Kalkylen utgår ändå från de gamla lamporna.” That is C. Arguing for the others: B names a real criticism but of a different claim — the August head-count is attacked in a separate move (“Augustibesöket bevisar inte heller det som tjänsteskrivelsen låter påskina”) and supports the “begränsat för flertalet motionärer” assertion, not the 38 000 figure; A is never claimed — the fixture count is not disputed, only which lamps are assumed; D is contradicted, since the author recomputes on the same span, “besparingen för två kvällstimmar”, matching the decision’s 21–23.

The closing programme is explicit: “för sommaren har nämnden faktiskt en poäng … Släck vid nio på sommaren, håll tänt till elva från oktober till mars”, which is B. Arguing for the others: A overshoots — the author concedes “mellan maj och augusti kan spåret gott släckas tidigt”, so he does not want 23:00 all year; C attributes a redirect-the-cut argument the text never makes — “Spartrycket är verkligt” concedes pressure but no other service is proposed for the cut; D is the position the whole column argues against.

Tennlöv's review is reported with hedges that the option preserves: "Men där källorna är fylliga nog att pröva saken tycks årplatserna ofta ha fördelats efter gårdarnas mantal", with "de största hemmanen närmast aktern". B is contradicted by "fördelningen återkom år efter år, så självklar att den sällan skrevs ned" and by "ordningen mest kom på tal när den var i gungning". A reverses the relation — the seat mirrors rank rather than conferring it — and D is never stated; the text says only "Styrmanstoften krävde väderkännedom, inte anor".

The author holds both readings open and declines to choose: "Samma rader kan alltså läsas som etikett eller som sjömanskap; protokollen skiljer inte mellan de två", and "Jag vet ärligt talat inte vad sätena visade". A and C both require him to settle the matter, which he explicitly refuses: "men den motsatta misstanken, att trimning och takt just var det språk rangen talade på vattnet, går inte heller att belägga". D reaches a similar conclusion for a cause the text never gives — the ground is the protocols' inability to separate the two readings, not any retouching of recollections.

The passage puts the lifting force in the few centimetres under the slab: her team “found dense mats of fine root, thickening year on year” there, and she says “Most of the force, we think, is generated within a hand’s width of the stone.” A fails because she does settle the location – the hedge “we think” is ordinary scientific caution, not an inconclusive core. C overstates: the deep ground held “almost nothing alive”, not nothing, and that is a secondary observation rather than the finding; D (anchoring roots cut in earlier repairs) is nowhere in the text.

Of the five, the text says: “They had been bedded to an older specification, on coarse sand laid nearly twice as deep as the current rule allows.” C is contradicted by the immediately preceding sentence “The five had one thing in common”, and B misassigns the water-main trench, which belongs to the single street that “failed and taught nobody anything”. A is contradicted too: the roots were found “riding clear over the crates beneath”, so the crates had not given way.

The twenty-five were never opened: only on the five “the flags were lifted”, while “The surveys measure the stones, and only the stones” and Askerholt insists “We are reading the flags, not the roots.” C is the trap – it asserts the mechanism the text explicitly refuses to claim, since “For all we know, the bedding on the good streets is filling with root that has not yet found its strength.” B is contradicted by the closing reading of “four millimetres, the same figure as the year before” (steady, not falling), and D is not addressed.

The writer delivers her own split verdict: “On the five streets Fearnbeck’s case is fairly won; on the twenty-five it is not.” Five of thirty-one is a minority, so he is mostly not borne out but vindicated on one count – roots did cross into the bedding sand there, and those pits were relaid “to Fearnbeck’s own specification”. C inverts the proportion; A is attributed to Askerholt’s group (“Askerholt’s group had thought his worry overdone”) and is undercut by the very next clause; D fails because that adjudicating sentence is the writer taking a side.

The article first explains the mechanism – “The slab shades the ground, waters it every clear night and lets it breathe. It builds the very thing that lifts it” – and then devotes most of its length to one city’s trial: “Thirty-one streets were rebuilt on cells”, surveyed “every April” for seven years. B is half right but mischaracterises the outcome: the new remedy has not failed, since “On twenty-five streets the celled flags have stayed within tolerance”. A is a first-paragraph supporting detail and D is never raised.

Fixed collocation: the only English idiom available is "takes its toll on", and the passage frames the dispute as a low-grade continuous drain — "deciding whose is a contest nobody admits to entering, though it quietly takes its ___(1)___ on the general mood". "take its price on" and "take its cost on" are not English (one pays a price, or something costs), and "takes its charge on" is meaningless in this frame. Only C yields a grammatical, idiomatic clause, so the rejected three fail on form, not merely on nuance.

The sentence is built on a concession: "The tone is light, but nobody misreads it; beneath the sponge the message is ___(2)___, and it is aimed at certain chairs." The "but" plus "aimed at certain chairs" demands a word meaning sharply and personally directed, i.e. "pointed". "relaxed" and "amused" destroy the contrast the "but" sets up (and a written message cannot itself be amused); "spirited" means lively or energetic, which neither opposes a light tone nor conveys targeting, so it leaves "aimed at certain chairs" unmotivated.

The clause quotes the idiom "the moral high ground": "you cannot hold the moral high ___(3)___ and a dripping brush at the same time", and "hold the high ground" is the fixed verb-noun pairing. "high horse" is a genuine idiom but takes get on / get off, never "hold the moral high horse"; "hold the floor" exists but means to have the right to speak, and "moral high floor" is not English; "high field" is not an idiom at all. Only A survives both the collocation with "hold" and the modifier "moral".

The preceding sentence sets up elapsed time — "So the kitchen waits. ___(4)___, somebody cracks – nearly always the same somebody" — so the connector must close the waiting, which is "Eventually". "Similarly" requires a parallel case and there is none, since "the kitchen waits" is a state, not a comparable instance. "Presumably" hedges, yet the writer immediately asserts observed regularity ("nearly always the same somebody, the one who minds the mess a little more than the rest"), so a supposition contradicts its own follow-up. "Ironically" would mark a reversal of expectation, but somebody finally cracking after a wait is precisely what the paragraph has been building toward.

"most kitchens ___(5)___ an uneasy balance between confrontation and squalor" is the collocation "strike a balance", and "uneasy" is that idiom's standard modifier. The other three take no balance object in English: one casts a vote or a shadow, deals a blow or a hand of cards, and lands a job or a punch. All three rejected options are therefore ungrammatical with "a balance" rather than merely weaker readings, leaving C as the only possible completion.

The passage says “whatever wet reached the torching sat against the battens until they decayed along its line”, which D restates. A claims the timber stayed sound, the opposite; B is contradicted because tiles “hang from two small lugs at the head, the nibs, hooked over each batten”; C overstates — torching stopped only “the fine snow, dust and draughts”, and “At that job it worked” limits the claim to that job.

Six middle-aisle pews were “marked vacant” in 1848 and four in 1849, and “In the plan of 1851 the vacant marks are gone” precisely when “Thin ruled lines now cut the boxes into single sittings” — the natural conclusion is that single lettings filled pews that would no longer let whole. A is undercut by those very vacancies, C speculates about poorer families with no textual support, and D misreads “two shillings apiece” per sitting as the price of a whole box.

The slaking is described directly: "Möter den brända stenen sedan vatten börjar den sjuda, spricker och faller sönder till ett fint vitt mjöl" — seething plus disintegration into a fine white powder, which is A. B is never addressed anywhere in the text; no ignition of wood by slaking heat is mentioned. C is contradicted by the storage account, "den brända stenen förvarades torr till dess den skulle släckas och blandas till bruk" — dry storage before slaking, not pits for maturing after it. D fails on its time clause: the sand enters only after the stone has fallen to powder ("faller sönder till ett fint vitt mjöl, den släckta kalk som blandad med sand ger murbruk"), never "medan den ännu sjöd".

The organisation paragraph states it outright: "En ugn var för stor för ett enskilt hushåll. Den restes och brändes av ett ugnslag – en handfull grannar som sköt till var sin andel ved, turades om vid elden och delade den färdiga kalken efter insats." That is D. A is contradicted head-on by "En ugn var för stor för ett enskilt hushåll". B invents an owner who charges for firing, whereas shares were settled in kind among equals — dagsverken "höggs in som skåror i en karvstock som följde ugnen" and the lime was divided "efter insats". C is contradicted by "Det mesta av kalken gick till avsalu" — most of the lime was sold, not kept for household use.

Two passages combine to give B: "för många hushåll var ugnen den binäring som över huvud taget gav kontanter" (an important sideline) and "Mot seklets slut tappade ugnslagen sin marknad" with "priset föll under vad ett lag av grannar kunde möta" (competed out). A inverts the stated priority: "Framför allt var det dit kalken gick: till murningen av stenhus, broar och kyrktorn", while only "något hamnade på åkrarna". C reverses the chronology twice — burning was long established ("hade bränningen sedan länge varit böndernas sak", with written evidence from the mid-1600s) and the railway lime works destroyed the trade rather than starting it. D is refuted by "Berget var däremot sällan något bekymmer, för i de här trakterna gick kalkstenen i dagen"; the binding constraint was firewood.

The remains are explicitly serial rather than contemporaneous: "inte sällan flera i rad utmed samma sluttning, äldre ugnar som övergivits när skogen omkring dem huggits ut, och som ersatts av en yngre ugn längre bort", so a tally of seventy rösen overstates how many were in operation at any one time — C. A misreads which boundary is meant: the kilns lie "i gränsen mellan inägor och utmark", a land-use border inside the farm, not a parish border. B is refuted by the reconstruction built "med handbokens kapitel och Gillervalls uppmätningar som förlaga" — the surveyed remains did yield how the kilns were built. D is the flat negation of "Hur gamla de äldsta lämningarna är går inte att avgöra utan utgrävning".

The stem asks about the besparingskalkyl specifically, and the text's charge against it is a single line: "Vintern 2023 byttes spårets gamla kvicksilverlampor mot ledbelysning" and "Kalkylen utgår ändå från de gamla lamporna" — that is C. B names a criticism the author really makes, but of a different claim: the August head-count is offered "som stöd" for the impact wording ”begränsat för flertalet motionärer”, and is attacked separately ("Augustibesöket bevisar inte heller det som tjänsteskrivelsen låter påskina"), not as an arithmetic flaw in the 38 000 figure. A is never advanced — the number of armaturer is never disputed, only their type. D is contradicted, since the author's recalculation uses the same two hours the decision covers: "stannar besparingen för två kvällstimmar på omkring tolv tusen kronor om året".

The closing paragraph concedes summer and demands winter reversal: "för sommaren har nämnden faktiskt en poäng: mellan maj och augusti kan spåret gott släckas tidigt, för då gör belysningen ingen nytta" and "Släck vid nio på sommaren, håll tänt till elva från oktober till mars" — exactly B. A overshoots: lighting until 23 all year round is precisely what the author gives up for May to August. C claims the cut is warranted but aimed at the wrong activity; the author never proposes saving elsewhere, only reshaping this decision seasonally ("Gör därför om beslutet i stället för att försvara det"). D is the position the whole piece argues against, from the opening scene of runners feeling their way back "på pannlampor och minne".

Om Tennlövs genomgång sägs: “där källorna är fylliga nog att pröva saken tycks årplatserna ofta ha fördelats efter gårdarnas mantal – de största hemmanen närmast aktern”, vilket C återger med samma förbehåll. B motsägs av att ordningen var “så självklar att den sällan skrevs ned” och “mest kom på tal när den var i gungning”. A vänder på orsaksriktningen – båten är “en flytande spegel av socknens rangordning”, inte det som avgör anseendet – och D:s roterande styrmansplats saknar stöd; om styrman sägs bara att toften “krävde väderkännedom, inte anor”.

Författaren lämnar båda läsningarna öppna: “Samma rader kan alltså läsas som etikett eller som sjömanskap; protokollen skiljer inte mellan de två”, och han slutar med “Jag vet ärligt talat inte vad sätena visade.” A och C förutsätter ett ställningstagande han uttryckligen vägrar göra – misstanken om inläst ordning “går inte att lägga undan”, men den motsatta “går inte heller att belägga”. D har rätt riktning men fel skäl: ovissheten kommer av att källorna inte skiljer etikett från sjömanskap, inte av tillrättalagda minnesbilder – vem som satt var beskrivs tvärtom som fast, “fördelningen återkom år efter år”.

findings.quote: Her cores could not settle where the lifting force was coming from.
findings.note: BLIND=PARTIALLY; PICK=B. Sibling stem q4 offers the option 'She agrees with Askerholt that the worry was overdone', which presupposes Askerholt holds a definite position, so A's null result is eliminable without the passage; D attributes the damage to earlier street repairs rather than to anything cores or digs found, so it does not answer the stem. That leaves B/C and B is the affirmative causal finding the unit is built on. Narrowing 4->2 passage-blind; the passage still decides B vs C.

findings.quote: A water main renewal, rather than the trees, seems to have disturbed them.
findings.note: BLIND=PARTIALLY; PICK=B (soft). B is the only option carrying an evidential hedge ('seems to have') and the only one explaining the five streets by an external cause, while A, C and D are all internal properties of the streets - a 3-vs-1 content split visible from form alone. No firm elimination is available, so this is a test-wiseness lean rather than a decided answer; recorded for adjudication.

findings.quote: The inspectors have measured their surfaces without examining the ground beneath.
findings.note: BLIND=PARTIALLY; PICK=A. The stem asks what is 'implied', which disfavours B (year-by-year gauge readings would be reported data, not an implication) and D (water uptake is a mechanism claim no other stem in the unit touches). A and C are mutually undercutting - if nobody examined the ground, C cannot be known - and an unstated methodological limit is the natural referent of 'implied'. Narrowing 4->2 passage-blind.

findings.quote: She sets out the dispute without taking a side of her own.
findings.note: BLIND=PARTIALLY; PICK=B (soft). D is the only fully neutral stance in a unit that stages a named objection plus trial results, and A is the total-dismissal extreme; both drop on option shape alone, leaving the mirrored qualified pair B/C. B and C are well balanced against each other and the passage decides between them, so this is narrowing, not answerability.

findings.quote: Why paving rises over tree roots, and how one city’s remedy has fared.
findings.note: BLIND=PARTIALLY; PICK=C. The sibling stems name Askerholt's findings, Fearnbeck's objection and a trial split into five and twenty-five streets, which rules out A (trip-hazard costs) and D (species replacement) without the passage; C is then the only option covering both halves the stems reveal (mechanism plus an evaluated remedy), where B commits to 'the remedies keep failing'. Main-idea options constrained by sibling stems is normal HP design, so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: It held the wet it took up against the battens, and the wood rotted there.
findings.note: BLIND=WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; PICK=D. Building-conservation knowledge decides this: lime torching is documented as taking up and holding moisture against the roof battens, causing batten decay, so a reader who knows the practice picks D with no text. B (torching steadying hung tiles) and A (torching sheltering the battens) are substantive competing claims about the same practice that a passage must settle, so this is world-knowledge answerability, not a structural leak.

findings.quote: whatever the weather drove against the roof
findings.note: Absolutizer strip, no expertise needed: C is the only option making an unrestricted claim ('the year round', 'whatever the weather drove against the roof') and is discardable on form alone, reducing the effective field to three before any domain knowledge is applied.

findings.quote: After 1851 a whole box in the middle aisle could be had for two shillings a year.
findings.note: Form mismatch, no expertise needed: the stem asks what can be 'concluded' about the letting of single sittings, but D is a bare price datum and is about whole boxes rather than single sittings, so it is eliminable on shape and topic alone.

findings.quote: Letting seats singly was the wardens' way of filling pews that would no longer let whole.
findings.note: BLIND=WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; PICK=B. Knowledge of nineteenth-century pew-rent economics (falling demand for whole pews, wardens subdividing boxes to protect income) points to B. A (excess demand) and C (provision for poorer families) remain substantive historical positions that the passage must decide, so world-knowledge answerability rather than a leak.

findings.quote: Stenen fräste och föll sönder till ett vitt pulver.
findings.note: blind class NOT_ANSWERABLE; blind pick null. A and B are both canonical facts about slaking quicklime (hissing disintegration to a white powder; heat sufficient to ignite dry wood), so domain knowledge ties rather than decides between them, and C and D are real adjacent practices (maturing pits, hot-mixed mortar). No option-cluster, no absurd distractor, no stem leak.

findings.quote: Att flera hushåll gick samman kring en gemensam ugn.
findings.note: blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick D. Swedish agrarian history (byalag, shared installations) makes the communal kiln the likeliest arrangement, but A (each farm eventually its own) and B (a well-off farm owning and charging) are substantive attested alternatives, so the lean is domain reasoning, not form.

findings.quote: Att kalken till största delen behölls för husbehov.
findings.note: C answers where the lime went rather than how the work at the kiln was organised, so it is soft-eliminable on stem fit; that is one elimination only, below the PARTIALLY bar.

findings.quote: Kalkbränningen var en binäring som växte fram först när järnvägarna kom.
findings.note: blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick B. Rural lime burning in Sweden long predates the railways, so C is world-doubtful, and D (limestone in the bedrock 'running out') is implausible as a cause of abandonment, leaving B ahead of A on historical grounds. C and D are substantive defeasible positions, so this is domain knowledge, not a structural leak.

findings.quote: Kalkbränningen var en viktig binäring som till sist konkurrerades ut.
findings.note: Round-4 shape check: the whole-arc channel is now honestly 1-in-2 — B and C share the 'Kalkbränningen var en (viktig) binäring som …' trajectory frame, so the former lone-whole-arc tell is gone, with A and D as the two non-arc claims. All four options are equally definite assertions, so no lone-hedge tell replaced it. No new mechanism.

findings.quote: Att antalet rester överdriver hur många ugnar som var i gång samtidigt.
findings.note: blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick C. The standard archaeological palimpsest caution (surface remains accumulate across time, so a count overstates simultaneity) makes C the likeliest inference, while B is doubtful because collapsed kilns usually do reveal something of their construction. B is a substantive competitor, so the tie-break is domain reasoning, not form.

findings.quote: Att lämningarna inte kan visa hur ugnarna en gång var byggda.
findings.note: Round-4 moderation check: the evidence-limiting channel is now honestly 1-in-2 — B and C both restrict what the remains can establish, against the two confident 'går att' claims (A, D). A form-only reader who discounts the ambitious claims lands on {B, C}, not on C alone. No new mechanism.

findings.quote: Den bygger på en enda räkning av löpare.
findings.note: blind class NOT_ANSWERABLE; blind pick null. A, C and D are three arithmetic objections to the savings calculation and are indistinguishable without the text; B is the sole methodological objection and the only option not opening 'Den räknar …', but that asymmetry points in no decidable direction and eliminates nothing, so it stays below the PARTIALLY bar.

findings.quote: Släckningen kan godtas på sommaren men bör hävas vintertid.
findings.note: blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick B. Swedish winter darkness plus the debate-article genre make the seasonal split the obvious measured stance, but C is a substantive competing debate move (concede the saving, contest where it is taken) and A/D are the two absolutes. Domain and genre lean, not form.

findings.quote: Neddragningen är visserligen befogad men görs i fel verksamhet.
findings.note: Round-4 moderation check: the concession channel is now honestly 1-in-2 — C's re-cut 'visserligen … men' concession matches B's 'kan godtas … men', so the lone-hedged-option tell is gone, with A and D as the unqualified absolutes. Seasonality crosscuts on a different axis (A and B), so no single channel isolates B. No new mechanism.

findings.quote: Att de största gårdarna ofta verkar ha fått platserna närmast aktern, där saken går att avgöra.
findings.note: Blind class PARTIALLY, blind pick C. C and A are a strength pair on one content axis (seat position tracks farm status): C is the hedged member ('ofta verkar ha fått' plus an explicit determinability caveat), A the absolute one ('avgjorde'), and the moderation heuristic picks the hedged twin using form alone.

findings.quote: Han finner både den sociala och den praktiska läsningen möjliga och avstår från att välja mellan dem.
findings.note: Three of q2's four options presuppose a contested status/hierarchy reading of the seats, which tells a passage-blind solver that the protocol finding must be a tentative status-linked seat pattern - corroborating C while stripping B (a records-keeping remark that feeds neither reading) and A (states the status reading as settled).

findings.quote: Han slår fast att hierarkiläsningen är en efterhandskonstruktion och att den bör överges.
findings.note: Blind class PARTIALLY, blind pick B. This option and A ('Han avfärdar rangläsningen ...') make the same move - rejecting the rank/hierarchy reading - so a form-only reader drops both as a mutually redundant pair, since two near-paraphrastic options cannot both be keyed; half the option space falls with no domain knowledge.

findings.quote: Han antyder att frågan knappast kan besvaras, eftersom minnesbilderna av vem som rodde var kan ha tillrättalagts i efterhand.
findings.note: The surviving pair is decided by two soft tells only: this option's grounds (retrofitted recollections) sit oddly against the documentary evidence base q1's stem establishes (protokollen), and B is the maximally balanced 'both readings possible' option that keys favour. Not decisive - the passage still separates B from D.

findings.quote: Their roots appear to have moved down into the loose loam below.
findings.note: Residual note, not a gate defect. Counsel's best case cites the paragraph-4 aside "the thin, stiff beds elsewhere were apparently not worth the climb" (which places the roots below the bedding on the twenty-five) plus Askerholt's premise that the cells "move the damp, aired horizon down and away from the stones". The case is beaten in-text by paragraph 5: "The surveys measure the stones, and only the stones" and "For all we know, the bedding on the good streets is filling with root that has not yet found its strength" explicitly deny that anything about the roots on the good streets is apparent, so key A stays clearly best; reattributing the paragraph-4 lift to "the crews" does not strengthen this option.

findings.quote: The mug among them is never anonymous: a name on the side, a chip everyone recognises, a teabag welded to the base, and an owner sitting twenty feet away, apparently unaware.
findings.note: CLEAN (round-4 check of the new paragraph-1 mug sentence): it touches no gap frame and no option. Gap (1)'s frame is intact and self-contained — 'deciding whose is a contest nobody admits to entering, though it quietly takes its ___(1)___ on the general mood' — the 'it' is bound inside its own clause to 'a contest', so the interposed mug sentence creates no new referent. None of the added words (name, side, chip, teabag, welded, base, owner, unaware) echoes any key (toll, pointed, ground, Eventually, strike) or any distractor across the five gaps; 'base' and gap (3)'s 'ground' are only loosely adjacent and sit in different paragraphs inside a fixed idiom. The addition also closes consistently with 'That colleague's mug, at least, is clean' — a different mug (the washer-up's), not the sink mug. On gap (1) itself all three distractors are CLEAN: 'takes its toll on' is the only idiomatic filler; 'takes its price/charge/cost on the general mood' is ungrammatical as a collocation.

findings.quote: horse
findings.note: CLEAN but the strongest lure in the item: 'high horse' is a real collocation, so C tempts. It dies on the frame — 'you cannot hold the moral high ___(3)___ and a dripping brush at the same time' — because 'the moral high ground' is the fixed phrase, one 'holds' ground (not a horse, which one gets on), and the parallel with 'a dripping brush' requires a holdable position. B ('field') and D ('floor') form no phrase with 'moral high'.

findings.quote: The boxes were divided mainly because more parishioners wanted seats than the church could hold.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: counsel's case — after division “names crowd where one household's name used to stand”, pew 9 “carries three surnames by 1856”, and “In 1861 the wardens raised the price of the front boxes to a pound” — crowding plus a price rise reads as demand outstripping supply. The case dies on the occupancy data at the moment of the change: “Six pews in the middle aisle are marked vacant that year, and four the year after” immediately precedes “In the plan of 1851 the vacant marks are gone”, and free benches stood at the west door — vacant pews contradict ‘more wanted seats than the church could hold’; the price rise is ten years later. Requires importing later data and ignoring the vacancies; attractive but beatable.

findings.quote: Kalken blandades med sand medan den ännu sjöd.
findings.note: CLEAN, strongest of the three: half of it is near-verbatim ('den släckta kalk som blandad med sand ger murbruk'), but the sentence labels the lime 'den släckta' — mixing follows completed slaking — and paragraph 3 fixes the order explicitly: 'den brända stenen förvarades torr till dess den skulle släckas och blandas till bruk'. The added 'medan den ännu sjöd' has no support. C is CLEAN (no maturing pits anywhere in the text; the only 'grop' is 'ofta med en grop i mitten' of a kiln cairn in paragraph 6) and B is CLEAN (world-true but the passage attaches heat only to the burning, never to slaking).

findings.quote: Kalkbränningen var en binäring som växte fram först när järnvägarna kom.
findings.note: CLEAN — round-4 check of the second whole-arc option; it dies on paragraph 7 and paragraph 1 as intended. Paragraph 7 shares the verb but not the subject: 'Vid järnvägarna växte kalkverk vars ugnar aldrig behövde svalna mellan satserna' — what grew at the railways was the industrial kalkverk that destroyed the peasant trade ('Mot seklets slut tappade ugnslagen sin marknad'), so the railways mark the end of the binäring, not its start. Paragraph 1 independently predates it: 'i socknar med kalksten i backarna hade bränningen sedan länge varit böndernas sak', as does paragraph 6's 'Skriftliga belägg för bränning i trakten finns från 1600-talets mitt, men tekniken är äldre än så'. It does not compete with key B and is not a second key. A is CLEAN on paragraph 2's 'Framför allt var det dit kalken gick: till murningen … och något hamnade på åkrarna', which contradicts 'i första hand'; D is CLEAN on paragraph 5's 'Berget var däremot sällan något bekymmer' plus paragraph 6's 'äldre ugnar som övergivits när skogen omkring dem huggits ut'.

findings.quote: Att lämningarna inte kan visa hur ugnarna en gång var byggda.
findings.note: CLEAN — round-4 check of the second evidence-limiting option; it dies on paragraph 8 as intended. The county museum rebuilt a kiln 'med handbokens kapitel och Gillervalls uppmätningar som förlaga', i.e. her measurements of the surveyed remains served as the template, which is a direct counter-example to an absolute 'inte kan visa'; paragraph 6 adds physical evidence of form ('låga, övervuxna rösen av rödbränd sten, ofta med en grop i mitten'). The 'no longer knowable' material in paragraph 8 is expressly scoped to firing practice — 'hur elden ska föras, hur länge, med vilken ved' — not to construction, which is the scope B tries to borrow. It is attractive but beatable on citation, and is not a second key. A is CLEAN because the text's boundary is the glossed 'gränsen mellan inägor och utmark', not parish boundaries; D is CLEAN on the verbatim negation 'Hur gamla de äldsta lämningarna är går inte att avgöra utan utgrävning'. Key C is anchored on 'inte sällan flera i rad utmed samma sluttning, äldre ugnar som övergivits … och som ersatts av en yngre ugn längre bort'.

findings.quote: Den räknar med fler timmar än beslutet omfattar.
findings.note: CLEAN — counselled hard on the 'omfattar' lure. findings.quote: Den bygger på en enda räkning av löpare.
findings.note: CLEAN, strongest distractor: the single August count is a real criticism in the text ('Augustibesöket bevisar inte heller det som tjänsteskrivelsen låter påskina'), but it is a separate criticism of the impact claim, not of the kalkyl the prompt delimits. The passage states outright what the kalkyl rests on — 'Kalkylen utgår ändå från de gamla lamporna' — so B misattributes rather than merely overreaching scope, and key C ('lampor som redan är utbytta') is the direct paraphrase. A is CLEAN: the text faults the lamp type, never the number of fixtures.

findings.quote: Neddragningen är visserligen befogad men görs i fel verksamhet.
findings.note: CLEAN — round-4 check of the re-cut concession; it dies on the right text and does not become a second key. A is CLEAN on 'året om' (paragraph 5 concedes summer switch-off); D is CLEAN because it is the position the text argues against, and the prompt asks what stance the text expresses.

Att defekten sitter i nyckeln och inte i en distraktor väger tyngre. Native: 'fräste och föll sönder till ett vitt pulver'.

findings.quote: priset föll under vad ett lag av grannar kunde möta

findings.quote: äldre ugnar som övergivits när skogen omkring dem huggits ut och ersatts av en yngre ugn längre bort

findings.quote: On the five streets Fearnbeck’s case is fairly won; on the twenty-five it is not.
findings.note: check (a) VERIFIED CLEAN, recorded not charged. The round-3 named-possessor verdict is a GENITIVE ('Fearnbeck's case is fairly won'), not the retired predicate-possessive scoring construction; 'are his' now occurs nowhere in this unit's passage or questions (the two file hits are repair_log provenance strings recording the fleet-repair-1 'from' wording, which is correct history-keeping), and the sole shipped bearer remains elf-b17-001's closing ('the findings that will outlast the trial are his'), so the >=2-batch retirement the disposition required still holds. No NEW shipped-bank echo: scanned every batch14-17 candidates-final passage plus all six batch18 siblings for "'s case", 'case is', 'fairly', 'fairly won', the fronted-PP semicolon antithesis and the trailing '; ... it is not' - zero bearers outside this unit. The OTHER shipped verdict formula was cleared too: 'X is right about Y' bears twice in the bank (elf-b16-001 'She is right about that', elf-b17-001 'Colverdine is right about the cheap part') and the repair correctly avoided it. elf-b16-002's 'It is not.' is a standalone flat negation in an unrelated construction, not this antithesis. Naming Fearnbeck also RAISES source-plausibility relative to the agentless round-2 form: a real feature writer names the man whose case it is, and the Pantheon exemplar carries exactly this kind of unattributed authorial evaluation ('Augustus wisely refused the honor'). Residual, carried and not re-charged: the shared THESIS SHAPE with elf-b17-001 (named male skeptic partly vindicated, scored by the writer) survives - but that is architecture, not construction, and fleet-repair-1's disposition retired the construction, expressly allowing 'any wording that keeps the partial-vindication content'.

findings.quote: And on five, when the flags were lifted, the crews found exactly what Fearnbeck had said they would find – mats of fine root in the bedding sand, riding clear over the crates beneath.
findings.note: check (b) VERIFIED CLEAN, recorded not charged. The reattribution keeps the survey/excavation scope distinction that P5's 'The surveys measure the stones, and only the stones' requires: the finding is now an EXCAVATION event ('when the flags were lifted, the crews found'), performed by the crews - a third, separately established actor (P1 'Crews grind the raised edges level') distinct from the April inspectors with their straightedge and wedge gauge and from Askerholt's research group. The unit now runs three clean actor roles (crews dig, inspectors measure, researchers core), so nothing in P4 credits the surveys with sub-stone knowledge and q3's key A ('The inspectors have measured their surfaces without examining the ground beneath') stands unthreatened - the lifting happened on the FIVE only, never on the twenty-five, so P5's 'For all we know, the bedding on the good streets is filling with root' remains true. It also repairs a causal gap the round-2 wording left open: a straightedge survey cannot see bedding sand, whereas flags taken up for relaying obviously can, and 'Those five have since been relaid on a thin mortar bed' now has its 'since' correctly anchored to the lifting. Chronology checked for doubling and inversion: bedded to the old spec (past perfect) -> flags lifted, roots found (past simple) -> since relaid (present perfect); 'and relaid' was rightly kept out of the reattribution clause, so the relaying is stated once and in the right order.

disposition: Round-3 passage edits pass this gate on all three checks; verdict moves from flag to pass because the single major that drove the earlier flag (rationale desync on q4's verdict quote) is closed and the round-3 edits introduce no new major. Standing dispositions carry unchanged: the 'are his' scoring construction stays retired for at least two batches (it is not re-created here), the years-credential appositive formula rests for the next batch, and the intra-batch '-holt' pair remains within tolerance with no further '-holt' coinages for two batches.
comparative_note: Read against the three ELF exemplars, elf-b18-001 sits comfortably inside the range rather than at its edge. host-2021-verb2-ELF-040 is the closest match in kind: a long expository feature built on named figures in disagreement, thick with measurements and dates, hedging its own conclusion while still letting the writer's judgement show - which is exactly the licence the repaired verdict sentence uses. The two short exemplars confirm the question register (bare HP prompt forms, options in paraphrase rather than passage strings), and the candidate's five prompts match that register. The round-3 edits move the unit toward the exemplars, not away: naming Fearnbeck gives the verdict the same authorial-but-embedded quality as the exemplar's 'wisely refused', and handing the bedding-sand finding to the crews restores the kind of concrete works detail the exemplars are full of.
